question.value: Are photometrically selected z>3 passive galaxy candidates in CANDELS truly passive (checked with archival ALMA sub-mm), and what are the stellar mass function and mass density of passive galaxies at 3<z<5?

evidence.quote: In the present work, we first confirm the passive nature of these candidates adopting the method presented in S19 and taking advantage of the richer ALMA archive
We then analyse the emergence and mass growth of this peculiar class of galaxies by means of two powerful statistical tools: the Stellar Mass Function (SMF) and the Stellar Mass Density (SMD).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: 2012.1.00869.S, 2012.1.00173.S, 2013.1.00718.S

bands.value: Band 6 and 7 used (Band 3 and 4 not used)

evidence.quote: A search in the ALMA archive returned observations in Band 6 and 7 for 41 of them.

We produced images with $\geq$0.6 arcsec spatial resolution using “natural” weightings and $uv$-tapers when needed.

method.value: Read pixel value at source position in natural-weighted tapered maps; uncertainty from std of pixels with similar coverage; max within beam if >3 sigma, mean within beam if undetected; weighted average of repeated observations

evidence.quote: The sub-mm flux was read directly on the map (in units of Jy beam$^{-1}$) as the value of the pixel at the position of the source.
In this way, we could assume that sources are unresolved (see justification and references in S19)

evidence.quote: We converted the inferred total infrared luminosity between 3 and 1100 $\mu$m adopting the calibration of (cite: kennicutt12), adjusted to a Salpeter IMF using their conversion factor.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute stepwise SMF and SMD, fit Schechter functions

results_numeric.quantity: Passive SMD increase z~5 to z~3

evidence.loc: 5 The SMF and the Stellar Mass Density
evidence.quote: An increase in the SMD of passive galaxies by a factor of 7 from $z\sim 5$ to $z\sim 3$ is observed.

evidence.loc: 5 The SMF and the Stellar Mass Density
evidence.quote: 20-25% of the total mass assembled by redshift $\sim$3 is accounted for by passive galaxies, while this fraction reduces to $\sim$5% at $z>4$.

findings_qualitative.value: No significant ALMA detection even in stacks; sample consistent with being passive on average

evidence.quote: No significant detection is found even after stacking all observations in the same Band

claims.hypothesis: The photometrically selected z>3 candidates are truly passive
claims.experiment: Archival ALMA Band 6/7 fluxes converted to SFR limits and compared to optical star-forming solutions and the Main Sequence
claims.result: 61% individually confirmed at 3 sigma; none rejected; sample on average passive

evidence.quote: we could not reject any of the candidates, and found that the sample is on average consistent with being correctly classified as passive.

claims.experiment: Stepwise SMF and SMD of passive galaxies in three redshift bins
claims.result: Strong evolution of M* beyond z~4; passive fraction >50% at high mass for z<4 but few percent at z>4
claims.finding: Epoch of passivization of massive galaxies near z~4

evidence.loc: 5 The SMF and the Stellar Mass Density
evidence.quote: we observe a pronounced evolution beyond $z\sim 4$, indicating that we are witnessing the epoch of *passivization* of massive galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Models reproduce observed high-z passive SMF
claims.experiment: Compare SMF, passive fraction and SMD with PANDA, TNG100/300, EAGLE, SIMBA
claims.result: No model matches over entire mass and redshift range

evidence.quote: none of the model analyzed is able to reproduce the observed passive galaxies over the entire mass and redshift range

why_this_data.value: Herschel stacking too shallow to reject mild SFR, so ALMA used

evidence.loc: 3 Confirmation of the passive nature of the candidates from their sub-mm emission
evidence.quote: is not sufficient to reject mild levels of SFR in these galaxies. For this reason we opted for ALMA data to confirm the passive solutions of our candidates.

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA data not deep enough to confirm or reject 39% of observed candidates; SFR depends on IR template

evidence.quote: Since the available ALMA data is not deep enough to draw any conclusion for 39% of the observed candidates
